haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC cron (attempt 1) starts it. It extracts rows with updated_at after hwm minus 2h and up to 02:00 UTC, all columns.
haiku-low.q2: A bulk-import row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at, and replica lag adds to that delay.
haiku-low.q3: The edit sets a newer updated_at. A nightly extract whose window covers it picks it up, and the merge replaces the loaded row.
haiku-low.q4: The delete is a write setting updated_at and deleted_at. The row is merged with is_deleted true and deleted_at set, not removed.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt is marked failed with its error and hwm is unchanged. Retry in 15 minutes. After attempt 3 fails, on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: They show the previous night's data. A separate 06:00 UTC staleness job posts an alert to Slack channel data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: Sunday reconciliation. It compares counts and checksums for the last 30 creation days, then reloads any mismatched day with the later-only merge.
haiku-low.q8: The merge replaces an existing row only when the incoming updated_at is later. Equal timestamps keep the copy already loaded.
haiku-low.q9: In ops.pipeline_state as hwm. It is set to the window end, only if it moves forward, in the same transaction as the merge and run status commit.
haiku-low.q10: The single warehouse commit: merge, hwm and run status land together. Dashboards read only analytics.orders, so they see all or nothing.
haiku-low.q11: Staged rows from earlier attempts are deleted when the next attempt starts. The retry uses the same window, since hwm is unchanged and the end is fixed.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads that day's rows with updated_at at or before hwm and applies them with the later-only merge in one transaction. Whether it moves hwm: NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: The 02:00 UTC cron starts attempt 1 (later attempts are started by the scheduler 15 min after a failure). It extracts rows from the replica's orders table with updated_at > (hwm minus 2h) and updated_at <= the night's 02:00 UTC run time. First run with no hwm row extracts the full table.
sonnet.q2: The document says a bulk-import row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at, and replica lag adds to that. It does not state why bulk imports are delayed.
sonnet.q3: The edit sets a newer updated_at, so the row falls in a later nightly window (or the 2h overlap). Staging then merges it into analytics.orders on order_id, replacing the existing row because the staged updated_at is later.
sonnet.q4: A delete is a write that sets deleted_at and updated_at, so it is extracted like any change. Staging sets is_deleted true, and the merge replaces the warehouse row (if updated_at is later) with is_deleted and deleted_at set. The row is not physically removed.
sonnet.q5: The transaction is rolled back, the attempt is marked failed with its error, and the hwm is unchanged. Next attempt starts 15 min later with the same window. If attempt 3 fails, on-call is paged and there is no further automatic attempt.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the previous night's data. The 06:00 UTC staleness job posts a staleness alert to the Slack channel data-alerts (and on-call is paged if attempt 3 failed).
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares count and checksum per creation day for the last 30 days, and reloads any mismatched day from the replica using the same later-only merge.
sonnet.q8: The merge replaces an existing row only when the incoming updated_at is later. Equal timestamps are treated as the same version, so the loaded copy is kept. The same guard is used in the fallback update plus insert.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table ops.pipeline_state. The value is the window end (the night's 02:00 UTC run time), not the max updated_at seen. It is set inside the single warehouse transaction with the merge and run status, just before commit, via UPDATE ... SET hwm = :end WHERE hwm < :end, so it only moves forward.
sonnet.q10: The merge, hwm update and run-succeeded status happen in one warehouse transaction that commits atomically. Dashboards read only analytics.orders, never staging, so they see a night only after the commit. A failure rolls back everything.
sonnet.q11: The next attempt deletes all leftover rows in staging.stg_orders from earlier attempts before loading its own extract. The retry extracts the same window, since the window end stays fixed at the night's 02:00 UTC and the hwm is unchanged.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads that creation day's rows from the replica (the doc does not say precisely which filter beyond reloading that day). It applies them with the same later-only merge in one transaction, never delete and re-insert; on error it rolls back. The doc does not say the reload touches the nightly hwm. It uses the committed hwm only as a cutoff for comparison, so it NOT STATED that it moves the hwm.
